verdict.summary: The selective-disclosure addition is correctly scoped as an opt-in delegation seam rather than an in-repo verifier. The implementation fails closed when no verifier supports the suite, delegates before producing a commitment, commits only the disclosed credential graph after acceptance, keeps the whole-credential and selective-disclosure token spaces separate, and attributes successful acceptance to the host verifier. The tests exercise the load-bearing real control paths: unavailable and unsupported verifiers do not ingest, rejection propagates without ingestion, acceptance commits exactly the disclosed triples, and inputs are forwarded unchanged. Documentation consistently disclaims selective-disclosure soundness, unlinkability, and external audit status, and the public-surface skill is updated. No correctness, soundness, test-validity, or security defect requiring changes is evident in the diff.
